title: Nasdaq-100 Futures Dip as Nvidia Sell‑Off Continues, Dragging Market Lower – Live Updates】
body:
Wall Street’s tech‑heavy Nasdaq‑100 futures slipped on Wednesday evening, pulled down by a fresh wave of selling in Nvidia after reports surfaced that the company’s board is contemplating a leadership change that could see CEO Jensen Huang removed. The dip came despite a broader rally across the three major U.S. equity indices, which were buoyed earlier in the session by a surge in cloud‑computing specialist CoreWeave and a brief rebound in Nvidia’s own stock after a previous slump.

The Nasdaq‑100 futures index, a forward‑looking gauge of the technology‑laden benchmark, fell about 0.8% by the close of trading. The decline erased much of the modest gains recorded earlier in the day, underscoring how quickly investor sentiment can swing on news of corporate governance turbulence at a marquee chipmaker. Nvidia’s shares, which had been climbing after a modest earnings beat, tumbled more than 5% after Bloomberg reported that insiders were discussing the possibility of a board‑led ouster of Huang, the founder‑CEO who has been synonymous with the company’s meteoric rise in artificial‑intelligence hardware.

Analysts say the market reaction reflects both the stature of Nvidia in the AI boom and the uncertainty that a leadership shake‑up would introduce. “Nvidia is the bellwether for the AI sector. Any hint of instability at the top reverberates across the entire ecosystem, from semiconductor suppliers to cloud providers,” noted Sarah Patel, senior equity strategist at Meridian Capital. “Investors are weighing the potential for a strategic pivot against the risk of losing the visionary guidance that has driven the company’s rapid expansion.”

The broader market rally that preceded the Nvidia wobble was anchored by a sharp uptick in CoreWeave, a smaller player that specializes in AI‑focused cloud infrastructure. The company announced a $2 billion financing round led by a consortium of venture firms, propelling its stock up more than 10% and providing a lift to the technology sector at large. CoreWeave’s surge highlighted the appetite for capital among niche AI service providers, even as the sector grapples with supply‑chain constraints and escalating competition for talent.

Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 managed modest gains, helped by solid earnings reports from industrial and consumer‑goods firms. Yet the Nasdaq’s underperformance illustrates a growing divergence: while traditional sectors are steadier, the tech-heavy index remains highly sensitive to news that can affect its marquee constituents. The episode also underscores the heightened scrutiny corporate boards now face as investors demand not only financial performance but also robust governance structures capable of navigating rapid technological change.

In the days ahead, market participants will be watching for any formal statements from Nvidia’s board or from Huang himself. A clear communication strategy could help stem the tide of sell‑offs, but lingering doubts may keep volatility elevated. Moreover, the episode may prompt other AI‑centric firms to reassess their own leadership succession plans, especially as the industry matures and the pressure to deliver consistent growth intensifies.

Looking forward, the trajectory of Nasdaq‑100 futures will likely hinge on whether Nvidia can quell the leadership speculation and re‑establish confidence in its strategic direction. If the board decides to retain Huang, the stock could rebound quickly, pulling the broader index higher. Conversely, a leadership transition could introduce a period of uncertainty that drags the tech sector lower, even as other parts of the market continue to post incremental gains. Investors will be keen to see how the narrative unfolds, with the broader implication that governance issues at high‑profile AI companies may become a new catalyst for market movement in the months to come.
